thread.title: Islanders players reflect on season after missing playoffs by seven points
thread.title_full: Islanders players reflect on season after missing playoffs by seven points

author: y. r. walker
title: Islanders players reflect on season after missing playoffs by seven points
text:
Captain Anders Lee said on Apr. 15 that the New York Islanders were disappointed and frustrated after their season ended early, missing the playoffs by seven points. Lee said, “We were in a really good spot. That’s a tough pill to swallow. Whether it was consistency or shooting ourselves in the foot, losing out on some points here and there. It’s a tight league. We had kind of our worst stretch at the worst time.”
The team’s late-season performance—a 4-10-0 run from March 19 onward—resulted in them falling out of playoff contention despite being in position earlier in the year.
Players gave several reasons for their struggles, including scoring difficulties and defensive lapses that put pressure on goaltenders Ilya Sorokin and David Rittich. Bo Horvat said, “It’s a mixture of things. I don’t think it’s from a lack of effort. Our scoring kind of ran dry a little bit, especially down the stretch when we needed it most.” Tony DeAngelo added, “We probably relied on [Ilya] Sorokin a little too much. Too many chances we gave him and stuff. You can’t expect a guy to just be the hero every night.”
The power play was another concern for players after finishing 30th in the National Hockey League with a conversion rate of 16.5 percent this season. Brayden Schenn said he felt “the pieces are there” for future success but emphasized better puck movement is needed during man advantages.
Despite disappointment, several players highlighted positives from the season such as rookie defenseman Schaefer tying an NHL record with 23 goals and Cal Ritchie becoming an NHL regular.
Mathew Barzal summed up team sentiment: “We’re pissed off in this room,” he said about missing playoffs this year but noted that caring deeply could become motivation moving forward.
